findings: surface flux depth is allocated to bins sequentially
existing fronts are advanced first and their storage demand is debited from available water
for a bin unsaturated at the surface, a dry-bin wetting-front advance Z_d is obtained by successive approximation using the Green-Ampt cumulative infiltration equation
the 2008 implementation description says these dry-bin Z_d values are stored for later unsaturated-bin injection
the newly created front storage is explicitly debited from the time-step infiltration volume

sources.role: improved finite-water-content method and preferred modern theoretical lineage
findings: Eq. 18 adds the K(theta_i) subtraction and uses right-edge bin hydraulic properties
mass conservation is imposed through explicit finite-volume accounting
rainfall is first added to the land surface, existing advancing bins then consume surface water, and only afterward can new bins take water
for new bins the initial advance is limited by the maximum advance during a time step as described in Talbot and Ogden 2008
the paper does not by itself establish that one time-independent stored Z_d table is the intended modern production representation
